$comment: INC-0924 / T-SAS-ORDER-PHONE-FIRST — the order of ACCEPT_PAIRING and the SAS prompt, and what the
data plane is allowed to do inside the window the new order opens. RESUME-PROTOCOL v3.0 RULE 30.
ONE file, TWO consumers:
tests/e2e-sas-order-contract.test.mjs                       (web: hooks/useE2e.ts sasPendingRef +
isSealedFrameType, hooks/phoneE2e.ts
viewAfterPairEnded[DuringSas],
lib/encryptedModeCopy.ts)
dnkdialer-android/.../E2eSasOrderContractTest.kt            (phone: PhoneService's accept ORDER,
E2eFrameGate, E2eSasGate.mayProceed)
THE INCIDENT. Until this build PhoneService called E2eSasGate.await BEFORE sendPairingDecision
('ACCEPT_PAIRING', ...). The computer derives its five digits from the e2e block inside that ACCEPT,
so the phone asked 'same code?' while the computer's screen was blank: 'the pairing code doesn't show
up in the CC webapp or extension before I confirm on the phone' (Dennis, 2026-09-24). Row
`phone-first-confirm` pins that ordering as FORBIDDEN — it is the only row here whose expected value
is that the product must NOT do something it used to do.
WHERE sasPending LIVES. Nowhere on the wire. It is not a field in the e2e block, not in the SPEC 13.3
transcript, and not a new frame: each side derives 'the code is not confirmed here yet' from its own
local state (phone: PhoneService.e2eSasPending; browser: useE2e sasPendingRef, keyed on
decision.effective, unchanged since P6.1c). The digits are therefore byte-identical to the ones the
frozen transcript produced before this change, and tests/sas-vectors.json is untouched.
`sealedOutbound` / `sealedInbound` are what the FRAME GATE does to a SPEC 13.7 sealed type in that
row's state, on the phone. `drop` is a DROP, never a plaintext downgrade: the pair is encrypted and
the user has been told so.
Asserted against the SOURCE of PhoneService.completeEncryptedAccept, because the accept path needs a
relay socket, a Keystore and a bound Activity and so has no JVM unit seam. A source-order assertion
is crude; it is also exactly the regression that shipped, and it goes red when the two statements
are swapped back.

rows.label: the OLD order: the phone waits for the user before the computer has any digits — now FORBIDDEN
rows.why: a comparison with one side blank is not a verification; it teaches the user to tap Matches on sight

rows.label: ACCEPT first, both screens show the same code, both users confirm
rows.note: phone values are AFTER the MATCH verdict clears the window

rows.label: inside the window: accepted, digits on both screens, nobody has confirmed yet
rows.why: a session exists and nobody has verified the peer; SEND_SMS and MAKE_CALL are sealed types the phone RECEIVES, so the window is closed in BOTH directions

rows.label: the phone's user answers "Doesn't match" after the ACCEPT
rows.why: the request is already resolved on the relay, so DECLINE_PAIRING names nothing; LEAVE_ACTIVE is the existing phone-initiated teardown and the relay answers it with PAIRING_TERMINATED

rows.label: the computer's user answers "Doesn't match"
rows.why: confirmSas(false) keeps the block ON (fail closed) and returns true, which is usePhoneBridge's existing revokeLocalPair -> RESET_ROOM; the phone's in-flight wait is cancelled by the teardown, and CANCELLED is a refusal

rows.label: nobody answers on the phone inside the 30 s pairing deadline
rows.why: silence is never a yes; it takes the same path as a refusal because downstream they must be indistinguishable

rows.label: the socket flaps while the code is on both screens and unanswered
rows.why: a resume re-forms the SAME pair, so the window is still open; the flag is cleared only by a MATCH or by the teardown that drops the session

rows.label: E2E_PAIRING_ENABLED=0 and the PHONE's local Encrypted mode ON — DOCUMENTED, NOT ENDORSED
rows.why: the relay refuses only mode=1 REQUESTS (server.js:1622); a mode=0 request is forwarded intact and the phone's local ON makes the pair verified by the SPEC 13.1 OR. So the kill switch does NOT stop a SAS-blocking pair. Pinned here so a change to that behaviour is a deliberate, reviewed change — see the open question in DISPATCH-BRIEF-FORGE-SAS-ORDER.md, which is Security's to rule on, not this lane's
